evidence: Exact 237-authored-control census: 189 physical activations, 33 intentional high-risk or unavailable-state skips, 15 disabled/derived/future-state blocks, zero failures or unclassified controls; 715 runtime-generated controls were audited separately below.

Network lifecycle, discovery, connection, shared-secret, join-import, and settings-save actions affect processes, external network state, credentials, or persisted config and were not executed by the hermetic census.

These explicitly authored future network actions are intentionally disabled and have no production handler in the current surface.

evidence: The root census discovered 206 authored controls including the 32-control app shell; this non-overlapping overlay credits only its 174 Home/Metrics/Diagnostics/Maintenance/Settings-save-dialog controls: 123 activated, 2 destructive skips, 49 blocked, zero failures or unclassified controls.

exception_groups.blocker: Verified matrix deletion is destructive and was neither armed nor executed by the disposable control census.
Backend shutdown changes process lifecycle and was not executed by the control census.
The route-specific backend effect requires its own isolated full-effect harness and was not invoked by this local-control census.
Opening an operator folder/file delegates to the OS shell and was not executed by the hermetic browser census.
Diagnostics recovery preview/reconcile requires lifecycle-specific isolated setup; reconcile can mutate backend evidence.
Diagnostics proof-pack, smoke-pack, strict-gate, and rerun actions require an isolated full-effect process harness.
These backend-owned refresh/support/preview actions are not local display transitions and require focused route-specific evidence.
Strict Settings save confirmation requires a staged patch and confirmation-specific harness; the root census did not manufacture a persistence candidate.
